title: Needlebench: microburst-aware lightweight load probe for PR perf gating
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: PR-level CI gates today are good at catching gross throughput regressions but miss short-duration microburst regressions and kernel-selection regressions that only surface at specific sequence-length distributions or after KV-cache warmup patterns. These flakier regressions can degrade p95 latency or tokens/sec for production traffic.

Goal: Ship a compact, deterministic 'needlebench' harness that runs as part of PR checks (lightweight), simulates microburst traffic with controlled KV-cache states and sequence-length stratification, and produces a reproducible fingerprint and delta metrics (tokens/sec, p95, p99, kernel selection histogram). The harness should be cheap (<= 30s runtime), run on ephemeral CI runners or shadow pods, and output an attachable artifact and gating signal for PR merges.

Scope: implement injector + orchestrator + analyzers: a minimal synthetic workload generator that: 1) orchestrates warm/cold KV cache transitions, 2) emits microburst patterns (bursts with low quiescent intervals), 3) stratifies by token-length buckets, 4) captures kernel selection traces and per-step token latency. Integrate with the existing PR gating pipeline to add an optional fast gate that fails the PR if a reproducible p95 drop exceeds threshold against a rolling baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Needlebench binary runs in CI in <= 30s wall time on a small ephemeral runner
Produces artifacts: summary metrics JSON, kernel-selection histogram, raw per-token latency trace
Gate decision computed deterministically using rolling baseline and threshold rules and emitted as CI status (pass/fail)
Artifacts are uploaded to CI storage and linked in PR checks; minimal dashboard shows needlebench history per-branch
False-positive rate measured on historical PRs is < 1% across last 200 merges
Integrations: GitHub PR status + Console perf dashboard link work end-to-end
implementation_steps: Prototype generator in Python using existing load harness codepath; add KV-cache warmup transitions
Add microburst pattern presets (short-burst, medium-burst, long-burst) and length bucket configs
Instrument runtime to emit a small kernel-selection histogram event and attach to artifact
Define deterministic seed and fixture model snapshot for run-to-run reproducibility
Wire artifact upload to CI artifact bucket and produce PR check summary with links
Add gate adjudicator logic that compares run to rolling baseline; implement configurable thresholds
Create lightweight dashboard in Console under perf-regression project to visualize needlebench runs
Run retrospective on last 200 merged PRs (replay) to estimate FP/FN and tune thresholds
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Lightweight vs exhaustive: keep runtime <=30s to avoid CI cost; accepts reduced statistical power by focusing on high-signal microburst slices
Deterministic fixtures: use a pinned small model snapshot to avoid noise from model differences; this may not cover all production models
Baseline freshness: rolling baseline window of 14 days chosen to balance stability vs adaptation; shorter window increases sensitivity to noise
Cache warmup emulation: fully reproducing server KV cache behavior is expensive; we emulate hot/cold transitions via explicit prefix sequences instead of full cache population to save time
Fail gating strictness: default gate is warn-only for first 2 weeks in order to gather telemetry and avoid blocking merges due to calibration issues
